also: it makes no difference to me

terms.gloss: it makes no difference, it’s neither here nor there
terms.grammar: adverb phrase, with esse, ferre or habēre
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. susque dēque, from Gellius: susque dēque ferre, “to take a thing calmly, not to care much what happens”
Traupman 104: that’s neither here nor there (a matter of indifference), susque dēque est
terms.comment: Literally “up and down”: whichever way it goes. Gellius (16.9, quoted by Lewis & Short) collects it from Laberius and Varro: susque dēque ferre, susque dēque habēre, to be indifferent to something.

sources: Lewis & Short: susque deque
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 104, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
